elements.quote: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we assessed the clinical accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of commercially available Ag-RDTs.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review and meta-analysis.

elements.quote: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we assessed the clinical accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of commercially available Ag-RDTs.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an explicit statement of the main objective (assessing clinical accuracy of Ag-RDTs).

elements.quote: We systematically searched multiple databases... for publications evaluating the accuracy of Ag-RDTs for SARS-CoV-2 up until 30 April 2021.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the inclusion criteria (publications evaluating accuracy of Ag-RDTs for SARS-CoV-2) but does not explicitly state exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: We systematically searched multiple databases (PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, medRvix, bioRvix, and FIND) for publications evaluating the accuracy of Ag-RDTs for SARS-CoV-2 up until 30 April 2021.
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the information sources (databases) and the date the search was last conducted (up until 30 April 2021).

elements.quote: We assessed heterogeneity by subgroup analyses, and rated study quality and risk of bias using the QUADAS-2 assessment tool.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the method used to assess risk of bias (QUADAS-2 assessment tool).

elements.quote: Descriptive analyses of all studies were performed, and when more than 4 studies were available, a random-effects meta-analysis was used to estimate pooled sensitivity and specificity...
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the methods used to present and synthesize results (descriptive analyses and random-effects meta-analysis).

elements.quote: From a total of 14,254 articles, we included 133 analytical and clinical studies resulting in 214 clinical accuracy datasets with 112,323 samples.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies (133) and participants/samples (112,323) and summarizes study characteristics (analytical and clinical).

elements.quote: Across all meta-analyzed samples, the pooled AgRDTsensitivity and specificity were 71.2% (95% CI 68.2% to 74.0%) and 98.9% (95% CI 98.6% to 99.1%), respectively.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes (sensitivity and specificity) with confidence intervals.

elements.quote: Across all meta-analyzed samples, the pooled AgRDTsensitivity and specificity were 71.2% (95% CI 68.2% to 74.0%) and 98.9% (95% CI 98.6% to 99.1%), respectively.
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted, and the abstract reports the summary estimate (71.2%, 98.9%) and 95% confidence intervals.

elements.quote: Sensitivity increased to 76.3% (95% CI 73.1% to 79.2%) if analysis was restricted to studies that followed the Ag-RDT manufacturers' instructions. Testing in the first week from symptom onset resulted in substantially higher sensitivity (83.8%...) compared to testing after 1 week (61.5%...).
elements.reason: When groups are compared (IFU-conforming vs non-conforming, first week vs later), the abstract indicates the direction of effect (increased/higher) and which group is favored.

elements.quote: Concerns of bias were raised across all datasets, and financial support from the manufacturer was reported in 24.1% of datasets. Our analysis was limited by the included studies' heterogeneity in design and reporting.
elements.reason: The abstract briefly summarizes important limitations, including risk of bias concerns and heterogeneity.
The abstract text provided (text_1 and text_2) ends with funding information and does not contain a general interpretation of the results or their important implications.

elements.quote: Funding: The study was supported by the Ministry of Science, Research and Arts of the State of Baden-Wuerttemberg, Germany... and internal funds from the Heidelberg University Hospital... Further, this project was funded by United Kingdom (UK) aid... and supported by a grant from the World Health Organization (WHO)... and a grant from Unitaid...
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the primary sources of funding for the review.

elements.quote: Weregistered the review on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD42020225140).
elements.reason: The abstract provides the register name (PROSPERO) and registration number (CRD42020225140).

elements.quote: Initial data from independent evaluations suggest that the performance of SARS-CoV-2 Ag-RDTs may be lower than what is reported by the manufacturers. In addition, Ag-RDT accuracy seems to vary substantially between tests [4-6]. ... Such evaluations differ widely in their quality, methods, and results, making it difficult to assess the true performance of the respective tests [7].
elements.reason: The introduction describes the current state of knowledge regarding Ag-RDT performance and highlights uncertainties regarding variability and quality of independent evaluations.

elements.quote: To inform decision makers on the best choice of individual tests, an aggregated, widely available, and frequently updated assessment of the quality, performance, and independence of the data is urgently needed.
elements.reason: The introduction explicitly explains the importance and need for the review to inform decision makers with an aggregated assessment.

elements.quote: While other systematic reviews have been published, they include data only up until November 2020 [8-11], exclude preprints [12], or were industry sponsored [13]. In addition, only 1 assessed the quality of studies in detail, with data up until November 2020 [7,11]. With our systematic review and meta-analysis, we aim to close this gap in the literature...
elements.reason: The introduction identifies existing systematic reviews, cites them, and explains the need for the current review to address gaps in data timeliness, preprint inclusion, and independence.
This is a diagnostic accuracy review, not a review of intervention effects, so the mechanism of action of an intervention is not applicable.
This is a diagnostic accuracy review, not a review of complex interventions, so a logic model for intervention components is not applicable.

elements.quote: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we assessed the clinical accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of commercially available Ag-RDTs.

This element applies specifically to reviews of intervention effects. The provided manuscript is a diagnostic accuracy systematic review, not an intervention review, making this element not applicable.

We considered cohort studies, nested cohort studies, case-control or cross-sectional studies, and randomized studies.
